guide.title: Neonatal Resuscitation
guide.lead: Most newborns only need drying, warmth and watching. About 1 in 10 need help to start breathing, and good ventilation fixes almost all of them. Get breaths in within the first minute; compressions and epinephrine are rarely needed.

sections.title: The first 30 seconds
sections.question: Term, good tone, breathing or crying?
sections.yes: Stay with the mother: skin-to-skin, dry, cover, hat. Watch breathing, colour and tone. Delay cord clamping at least 60 seconds.
sections.no: Warm, dry and stimulate. Position the head neutral ("sniffing"); clear secretions only if they block the airway.

steps.title: Not breathing, gasping, or HR below 100
steps.text: Start PPV within 60 seconds of birth: 40–60 breaths/min at 20–25 cmH₂O. Room air (21%) at 35 weeks or more; 21–30% under 35 weeks. Pulse oximeter on the right hand.

steps.title: Is the chest rising?
steps.text: If not, MR. SOPA: Mask seal, Reposition, Suction, Open the mouth, Pressure up (to 40 cmH₂O at most), Alternative airway.

steps.title: HR below 60 after 30 seconds of breaths that move the chest
steps.text: Compressions: two thumbs on the lower third of the sternum, one-third of the chest depth, 3:1 (90 compressions and 30 breaths per minute). Oxygen to 100%. Recheck HR every 60 seconds.

steps.title: HR still below 60
steps.text: Epinephrine and, if blood loss is likely, volume.

doses.note: 0.1 mg/mL; every 3–5 minutes. Via ET tube 0.1 mg/kg while access is obtained

steps.title: HR 60 or more
steps.text: Stop compressions. Keep ventilating until HR is 100 or more and the baby breathes.

sections.title: Pre-ductal SpO₂ targets (right hand)
notes: Healthy newborns take about 10 minutes to reach normal saturation. Blue hands and feet (acrocyanosis) are normal at first.

sections.title: Keep warm (36.5–37.5 °C)
items: Dry, then remove the wet towel
Skin-to-skin on the mother, cover both, hat on
Under 32 weeks: plastic bag up to the neck without drying, then a hat

sections.title: Airway sizes
notes: Tube depth at the lip: weight in kg + 6 cm.
A size 1 laryngeal mask works from 34 weeks or 2 kg.

sections.title: Don't
items: Routine suction of the mouth, nose or trachea, including for meconium
Slap, shake or hold the baby upside down
100% oxygen for the first breaths of a term baby

items.label: Bradycardia
items.sub: In a newborn, slow heart rate means poor breathing: ventilate first.

quiz.q: After drying and stimulating, a term baby has poor breathing and HR 80. Next?
quiz.explanation: HR below 100 or poor breathing means PPV. Compressions only if HR stays below 60 after 30 seconds of good breaths.

quiz.q: 32 weeks, breathing, HR 110, blue hands and feet, pink body at 2 minutes. Best care?
options: Keep warm and monitor SpO₂ against the minute targets
quiz.explanation: Blue hands and feet are normal early. Breathing with HR 100 or more doesn't need PPV.

quiz.q: HR stays at 50 after 30 seconds of PPV that moves the chest. Next?
options: Compressions at 3:1 with 100% oxygen; prepare epinephrine
quiz.explanation: Epinephrine if HR is still below 60 after compressions and ventilation.

quiz.q: Starting oxygen for PPV in a term baby:
quiz.explanation: 21–30% under 35 weeks; titrate to the SpO₂ targets.

quiz.q: IV/IO epinephrine dose for a newborn:
quiz.explanation: 0.1 mg/kg is the ET-tube dose, not the IV dose.

quiz.q: A 29-week baby should be kept warm by:
options: A plastic bag up to the neck without drying, plus a hat
Drying vigorously and a blanket only
A cold room to reduce oxygen use

quiz.q: No chest rise during PPV despite a good mask seal. First fixes?
options: Reposition the head, suction if blocked, open the mouth, then raise the pressure
quiz.explanation: MR. SOPA: compressions without ventilation won't help.

quiz.q: Stop chest compressions when the heart rate is:
quiz.explanation: Continue PPV until HR is 100 or more and breathing is effective.

flashcards.question: Fetal shunts at birth
flashcards.answer: Ductus venosus, foramen ovale, ductus arteriosus. Breathing lowers lung pressure: the foramen ovale closes and the ductus arteriosus starts to constrict.

flashcards.question: Newborn resuscitation sequence
flashcards.answer: Warm, dry, stimulate, position. Apnoea or HR below 100 → PPV within 60 seconds. HR below 60 after 30 seconds of good breaths → compressions 3:1. Still below 60 → epinephrine.

flashcards.question: Preventing hypothermia
flashcards.answer: Dry, remove wet towels, skin-to-skin, hat, room 23–25 °C. Under 32 weeks: plastic bag up to the neck. Target 36.5–37.5 °C.

flashcards.question: PPV settings
flashcards.answer: 40–60 breaths/min, 20–25 cmH₂O to start, room air at 35 weeks or more. Watch for chest rise; no rise → MR. SOPA.

flashcards.question: Newborn compressions
flashcards.answer: Two thumbs on the lower third of the sternum, one-third of the chest depth, 3:1 (90 compressions and 30 breaths per minute). Oxygen to 100%.

flashcards.question: Meconium
flashcards.answer: Vigorous baby: routine care. Floppy baby: start PPV within the first minute. Routine tracheal suction is no longer recommended; suction only if the airway is blocked.

flashcards.question: Newborn epinephrine
flashcards.answer: 0.02 mg/kg IV/IO (range 0.01–0.03 mg/kg) of 0.1 mg/mL, every 3–5 minutes, if HR stays below 60. ET tube: 0.1 mg/kg.

flashcards.question: Newborn ET tube size
flashcards.answer: Under 28 weeks 2.5 mm; 28–34 weeks 3.0 mm; over 34 weeks 3.5 mm. Depth at the lip: weight in kg + 6 cm.

critical.scenario: Born at home 5 minutes ago, term, covered in thick green fluid: floppy, not breathing, HR 70 after drying and stimulating.
critical.question: Priority sequence?

options.t: PPV now (40–60 breaths/min, room air), check chest rise; suction only if the airway is blocked; compressions if HR stays below 60 after 30 seconds of good breaths
Intubate and suction the trachea before any breaths
options.f: No longer recommended: it delays ventilation.

options.t: Keep stimulating until the baby cries
options.f: Stimulation alone wastes the first minute.

critical.explanation: Ventilation is the most important step; keep the baby warm and transport with the mother.
critical.kpi: Starts PPV promptly in a non-vigorous meconium-stained newborn

critical.scenario: 35 weeks, limp and apnoeic. After 30 seconds of PPV at 20 cmH₂O, HR is 55 and the chest isn't rising. The mask seal looks good.
critical.question: What next?

options.t: Fix ventilation first: reposition, suction if blocked, open the mouth, increase pressure (up to 40 cmH₂O), consider an alternative airway – then reassess HR

options.f: Without chest rise, compressions won't oxygenate the heart.

critical.explanation: Compressions start only after 30 seconds of breaths that move the chest.
critical.kpi: Applies MR. SOPA ventilation corrective steps before escalating

critical.scenario: 32 weeks, born at home, room 17 °C. Breathing with mild nasal flaring, HR 110, pale, thin translucent skin.
critical.question: Biggest threats and priorities?

options.t: Hypothermia, breathing problems and low glucose: plastic wrap or skin-to-skin with a hat, warm ambulance, SpO₂ monitoring, CPAP or PPV if breathing worsens, check glucose, neonatal centre

critical.explanation: Cold preterm babies die more often; warmth is the first treatment.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes thermoregulation and monitoring in a preterm newborn
